title: Full character weights of conjugation
statement: Let $k$ be any field and $i:T\to G$ a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme]. Use characters $\chi:T\to\mathbf G_m$ and Laurent-coordinate evaluation [def-sfb-rank-one-root-interfaces], dual numbers and tangent points [sk-d-tangent]. For a commutative $k$-algebra $B$ and $b\in B$, define $s_b:k[\epsilon]\to B[\epsilon]$ by $a+c\epsilon\mapsto a+bc\epsilon$, with coefficients mapped to $B$. Define the full character conjugation weight space $\mathfrak g_\chi$ as the $k$-span of the vectors $v\in\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ such that, for every $B$ and $t\in T(B)$, $i(t)\,s_1(v_\epsilon)\,i(t)^{-1}=s_{\chi(t)}(v_\epsilon)$ in $G(B[\epsilon])$, where $t$ is extended constantly to $B[\epsilon]$. This tests full characters on all algebra points, including nonreduced algebras, rather than their differentials or values only on $T(k)$.

source.place: Section 4.1, character weight decomposition; Corollary 5.2.7(2), p.155
